summary: The note explores how trickster figures from ancient folklore (Coyote, Loki, Prometheus, Anansi) are reimagined in modern-day tales and parables, using a series of dated 2023-2024 vignettes involving tech moguls, animals, hackers and hoaxers. Each story is framed as a parable about power, technology, ownership, collaboration or misinformation. The note concludes that trickster lore endures as a mirror of society's foibles.
one_line: Modern trickster tales, from a Silicon Valley fox to a hacker Prometheus and a moon hoax, show how ancient trickster archetypes reflect today's society.
key_facts: Tricksters appear across cultures, from the shapeshifting coyote spirit of Native American lore to Loki of Norse mythology.
On October 15, 2023, a virtual symposium headlined by Dr. Nathaniel Thorne of the University of Ingenious Narratives examined the evolution of the trickster.
Felix Foxworthy, a tech mogul, announced on November 3, 2023 a plan for "GrapeNET", an interconnected web of grapevine ownership, quipping "It's all sour grapes until you control the vineyard."
On December 14, 2023, a coyote was photographed hitching a ride atop a self-driving Tesla; the photo went viral and the coyote was called a patron saint of disruptive innovation.
Janine Green, the Tesla's driver, became an overnight sensation and said to always "check your roof before you autopilot away!"
Video footage of a raven gathering surfaced online on September 22, 2023, with some believing the birds were exchanging information in an interspecies network.
Mia Crowell, an avian behavioral scientist, joked that ravens could soon hack into Zoom meetings.
Hacker Sam Sparks redistributed wealth from large corporations to the less fortunate on February 1, 2024, and is cast as a digital-age Prometheus who steals data instead of fire.
On January 5, 2024, an anonymous satirist pen-named Ana Nsi began a blog recasting the West African trickster-god Anansi as a modern blogger.
Jared Jest, a provocateur, orchestrated a hoax on March 30, 2024 convincing the world that the moon had split in two, illustrating societal gullibility and the spread of misinformation.
Prometheus in ancient Greek mythology was the rebel titan who stole fire from the gods and gave it to mankind.
The note concludes that trickster lore preserves questioning, defiance and the celebration of underdog cunning.
